findings.evidence: At 95690c28, RackDuplicarCommands.cs:290-321 (PlaceDestination) calls InDocumentTransaction.Run (InDocumentTransaction.cs:32-40: LockDocument, then StartTransaction, body, Commit). Inside it: RackCloner.CloneDefinition (RackCloner.cs:29-67: new BlockTableRecord, DeepCloneObjects, RackBlockData.Write of the restamped payload), then new BlockReference with Rotation, ScaleFactors = source.Scale and LayerId, AppendEntity. That is several definitions and references, atomic, with one Commit. RackLayoutCommands.cs:243 also calls CloneDefinition. All of these files are byte-identical between 3375aadb and 95690c28. Neither V2.1..V2.5 nor BA-06 V6 mentions RACKDUPLICAR or RackCloner. The error comes from the Gate 2 CONTRACT evidence (reviews[4].facts[12]: 'a first production caller-owned CREATION scope (RACKPROYECTAR)'), and V2.6 inherits it. This matters for the mirror in particular: the duplicate scope copies ScaleFactors, so it can carry a reflection. It is the structurally closest product form to a copy-provenance mirror.

rulings.item: AQ-V6-01 (where the AR5-12 detection of the BA-06 V6 §2.1 route pairs and the BA-08 V6 §3.2 W/C pairs lives)
rulings.recommendation: RULE (b): a dedicated per-build precondition checker. It is execution-preparation tooling in the custody of BA-07, not a baseline artifact: it has no BA-11 §3 entry and no DEPENDS_ON edge. Reject (a), where BA-03 absorbs the pairs, and reject placing the detection in BA-11. Content of the ruling: (1) Reading of AR5-12. It fixes the function (fail-closed detection of every cited pair against the build source SHA). 'El runner de BA-03 lo detecta' is read as 'the BA-03 runner detects its own pairs'; the detector of the union is the precondition checker. This is a reading and needs no errata, because AR5-12 was itself a reading. (2) Normative home. BA-07 §5.4 defines the checker's obligations, with BA-11 §3.2 row 'per-build bound-SHA precondition' as a pointer. The obligations: take the pair set from the sealed bytes of BA-03, BA-06 and BA-08, and verify first that their hashes equal the sealed hashes of BA-11 (`citingArtifacts`). The set is the union of: the BA-03 §2 BOUND rows; every BA-06 §2.1 code row except those declared precedent or outside the AR5-12 set (route rows, plus the residual and quantity sources conservatively); and the BA-08 §3.2 W and C rows. P rows and the FIXTURE_CONSTRUCTION_BUILD are excluded (FXB-03, AR6-04). The checker resolves each path at the bound SHA and at the build source SHA only; it does not use origin/main (see BA03V6-N1). It fails closed on any unequal or absent blob, any row it cannot parse, a pair count different from the count the reviewer declares, or a citing-file hash mismatch. It reports equality per resolution. (3) Evidence. The BA-07 §5.4 record carries the checker identity (path, sha256) and its output, in `runnerOutput` re-pointed or in a renamed field, and cites the BA-03 runner output run with the same build SHA. (4) Timing. The checker is written and reviewed at execution preparation, after the seal, because it reads sealed bytes. Its existence is not a baseline prerequisite: the precondition record is already NOT PRODUCED in BA-11 §3.2.
rulings.reasoning: BA-11 V6 §2.1 has BA-06 -> BA-03 and BA-08 -> BA-03 (seal order BA-03 before BA-06 and BA-08). If BA-03 carried the BA-06 and BA-08 pairs, a normative value of BA-03 (its expected identities) would be defined in BA-06 and BA-08. That adds BA-03 -> BA-06 and BA-03 -> BA-08, a cycle outside the single declared exception, and it would force a new BA-03 version for every BA-06 or BA-08 change. BA-11 is acyclic-safe because it is last, but its §3 is registry state and not procedure, and §§1..2.1 are the rule-5 agreed text, which should not grow a runner. AR5-12 itself places the precondition in 'preparación de ejecución por cada build bajo prueba' and puts the result 'con la tupla bajo custodia de BA-07'. A checker owned by execution preparation and recorded in BA-07 §5.4 is therefore where the contract points. Under BA-11 §2.1 a pointer to other artifacts is 'an informative pointer ... not a dependency', so BA-07 can specify the obligation without an edge. The pairs are data read at run preparation from sealed bytes, and no value of BA-07 is defined by them. BA-03 V5 already states the limited coverage (§8, §8.1), so no BA-03 byte changes.

No new IN_USE field, no tuple field, and no change to the vector or model of 4.1. Three conditions apply, all text-only in BA-07 V7. rulings.reasoning: AR5-12 sets the precondition 'por cada build bajo prueba'. AR5-12 assigns fail-closed detection to a runner, not to the custody verifier. A new IN_USE field would only move the U6 check into 6.2 step 5, at the cost of a new entry schema, a new vector and new cases. The same trade-off was accepted for U5 under AR4-06 (4) and AR5-04, whose condition (1) placed the citation in RUN_START, not in custody. I tried to refute this ruling recommendation and could not. Every check was read-only and ran in the worktree at 33ee9d5d.

(1) Delta V5 to V6. I diffed blob 0289cfbd against 569b5b04 (docs/initiatives/I-52-ct21d-baseline-ba-11-hash-registry-v5.md vs -v6.md). Inside §§1..2.1, only two rows changed, both in §1: the composite row, which adds "a later errata document's row governs over the earlier ones by its own section 0", and the identity row, which adds "and the section 0 of every later errata document". §2, the rules, the edge list, the seal order and §2.1 are byte-identical. This fits 223.4 ("§§1..2.1 idénticas byte a byte salvo lo que exija V2.6") and AR6-06.

(2) Section hashes. I sliced the text from "## 1. Hash procedure" up to "## 3. Registry entries" after LF normalization.
- V5 without the informative line gives 361a94f7…37aa, which matches AR5-15, so the method is reproduced.
- V6 gives c0a82084…4765 without the line and 81199f10…3f24613 with it. Both match the claim.

(3) Graph check. I re-ran I-52-ct21d-ba11-v5-graph-check.py against V6 and got ALL_PASS. The output SHA-256 is 59a176a3…a4de, the same as the committed v5 and v6 JSON files. The checker's LF hash is eebcf37b…fe8c.

(4) The two defects are real and stay within §§1..2.1.
- Rule 3 still reads "textual verification of V2.4 and V2.5" and leaves out V2.6.
- V2.6 D-1 (line 89) says the BA-11 version that the BA-01 candidate ruling cites "must name V2.6's row". BA-11 V6 §1 names that row only generically, not V2.6 explicitly.
Both are word-level fixes: in BA-11, or for D-1 possibly in V2.6.

(5) Conditions and sequence. Making the agreement conditional on V2.6 pre-approval plus textual verification matches AR6-06 and V2.6 §4. A V2.6 revision changes §4 and the composite, which are outside the agreed text. Because the agreement comes after V2.6, the cited blob will match the one the BA-01 candidate ruling cites, as AR3-25 and reading (5) of §218 require.

Caveat, not grounds for refutation: the AQ-V6-01 and AQ-V6-BA07-1 rulings must not add a DEPENDS_ON edge, or §2.1 would change after the agreement and reopen candidates. Moving detection into BA-03 is already excluded because it would create a cycle, and the §3.2 row places the precondition record in BA-07 custody as a review record, not as an edge. The record should confirm this.

I could not verify that findings BA11V6-01 and BA11V6-02 exist, because the review report is not in the files I read. The defects they describe are confirmed above.

votes.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. I checked it against the worktree at 33ee9d5d.

(1) What changed between V5 and V6 in §§1..2.1. I diffed V5 against V6 from the start to "## 3. Registry entries". Apart from the header and version lines, which are outside the agreed sections, only the two §1 rows changed: the composite-row precedence sentence gained "a later errata document's row governs over the earlier ones by its own section 0", and the identity row now reads "...and the section 0 of every later errata document cite". §2, §2.1, the edge list and the seal order are byte-identical. §223.4 allows this ("§§1..2.1 idénticas byte a byte salvo lo que exija V2.6").

(2) Hashes. I used the AR5-15 method: take the git blob, strip CR, take the text from "## 1." up to "## 3. Registry entries", and drop the single line starting "*Informative (not part of the agreed text)". Results:
- V5 gives 361a94f7…37aa, which matches AR5-15.
- V6 gives c0a82084…4765 without the line and 81199f10…4613 with it.
- The V6 blob is 569b5b0428a92bb477bf268fa88e9d75c4a5fe94.
- The checker I-52-ct21d-ba11-v5-graph-check.py is eebcf37b…fe8c.
- Re-running the checker against V6 exits 0 with ALL_PASS. Its output is 59a176a3…a4de, identical to the committed v6 json. The committed v5 json blob also hashes to 59a176a3; the checker output does not encode the registry path or blob, which is why the agreement record must cite the blob separately. The ruling already does.

(3) The two defects the ruling names are real, they sit inside §§1..2.1, and they are fixes at the level of individual words:
- Rule 3 in §2 still reads "the Coordinator's textual verification of V2.4 and V2.5 and the agreement of the effective contract". It omits V2.6, but under AR6-06 V2.6 must be verified before the effective contract is agreed.
- V2.6 D-1 says "the BA-11 version that the BA-01 candidate ruling cites must name V2.6's row". The V6 §1 rows use only a generic "later errata document ... by its own section 0" and name "section 0" but not D-1 of later errata documents. So D-1 and the V6 rows do not match. Substantively V2.6 §0 does hold the precedence row, so the generic wording works; the problem is that the texts are not aligned.

Both fixes count as "lo que exija V2.6" (§223.4, AR6-06), so they are allowed. Because no rule-5 agreement or candidate exists yet (§224(3)), fixing the blob in place reopens nothing.

(4) The forward claim holds. A V2.6 revision ordered in the pre-approval changes the V2.6 blob, and therefore BA-11 §4 and the composite. §§1..2.1 are version-generic and cite no contract blob, so they stay unchanged. The only exception would be a revision that moves V2.6's precedence out of its section 0, and nothing on record orders that.

Conditions the ruling already respects:
- AR6-06: the agreement comes only after V2.6 is pre-approved and textually verified.
- AR4-22: exact delta check and re-run on the corrected blob; the record cites the blob, the LF §§1..2.1 hash, the checker hash and the output hash, which is also rule 5 of V6.
- AR5-15: the agreement is recorded together with the first candidate ruling.

Non-blocking notes, both outside the agreed text:
- The informative line in V6 §2.1 still names the v5 output json path, while the V6 output was committed as ...-v6-graph-check.json.
- AR4-22 wants an exact delta check of the corrected blob, not just a re-run of the checker. The ruling implies this but should say it.

The ruling is supported. The severity of the underlying defects is minor.
